feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 8 PM this
evening to 8 PM EDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 28 at 3:14PM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39 PM
Friday 10/30, and 1.1 feet above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 28 at 12:20AM PDT until October 31 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

extended beyond Thursday.

St Johns River Near Astor and Deland affecting Lake and Volusia
Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The
river at Astor continues in Moderate flood while the river at Deland
is forecast to reach Minor Flood Stage this afternoon or tonight.
Water levels at both sites are forecast to begin a slow decline late
this week and weekend.

For the St. Johns River at Astor...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the St. Johns River near Deland...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Docks and piers are completely submerged at
Pier 44 Marina. Many docks are partially submerged at Hontoon
Landing Marina.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Tuesday the stage was 3.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.0 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low
lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.3 feet MLLW at
the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From noon to 3 PM PDT Wednesday. High tide is at 1:13 PM

will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

properties.areaDesc: Kittitas Valley
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog has been observed in the Kittitas Valley early
this morning, especially notable along I-90 west of Ellensburg.
Within fog, visibilities as low as one-quarter mile are expected
to persist into morning. Use extra caution while traveling as
visibilities can change quickly. If fog is encountered, use low-
beam headlights and keep plenty of space between you and other
vehicles.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39
PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 26 at 8:59PM PDT until October 30 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8
to 13 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday evening. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT early this morning.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 8 PM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 27 at 1:22AM EDT until October 28 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 26 at 1:39AM EDT until October 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent and gusty northeast winds are slowing river flow. The St
Johns River at Astor will remain in Moderate Flood Stage, though
river levels are forecast to slowly decline through this weekend.

forecast.

forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.

at 8:30 PM EDT Tuesday was 3.8 feet.

just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 2:40AM EDT until October 31 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 29 at 2:56AM EDT until October 29 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds are causing river levels to rise on
the St Johns at Astor, currently in Moderate Flood Stage. The river
is forecast to remain in Moderate Flood Stage, perhaps beginning a
slow decline late week into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Monday the stage was 3.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Monday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.8 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at
12:15 PM Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at
12:56 PM Wednesday 10/28, 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at
01:43 PM Thursday 10/29, and 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW)
at 02:39 PM Friday 10/30. These predictions include up to 1.2
ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.

tide is expected to be 2.1 ft above normal (7.9 ft MLLW) at

ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and
flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or
later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco
Bay, respectively.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent gusty northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are
slowing river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are
forecast to begin a slow decline late this week, but remain in
Moderate Flood stage for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland, Astor...Moderate flooding
is forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road

homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to crest around 3.8 feet
this week, then begin a gradual decline late in the week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.

afternoon. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Sunday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 2 PM this afternoon to 8 AM
EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 at 2:01AM EDT until October 31 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 25 at 3:16PM EDT until October 28 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.

Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds and upstream tidal effects are slowing
river flow on the St Johns River at Astor. River levels are forecast
to slowly decline into the weekend but remain in Moderate Flood stage
for at least the next couple weeks.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue
Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter,
Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 3.8 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast to begin a gradual decline
through late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in
low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. Up to one half foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near
shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.0 and 9.3 feet MLLW
at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...From noon to 3 PM PDT Wednesday. High tide is at 1:13
PM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater
inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high
tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures
expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in
the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon.

properties.areaDesc: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches, Santa Barbara County
Central Coast Beaches, Santa Barbara County Southwestern
Coast, Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be through
Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal Flood
Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf develops.
The Coastal Flood Advisory may also need to be extended beyond
Thursday.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 28 at 7:54PM EDT until October 29 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San
Francisco Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. More substantial impacts are expected along bayshore
Marin County where increased flooding is anticipated across
low lying areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 01:43 PM
Thursday 10/29, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 02:39 PM
Friday 10/30, and 1.1 feet above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
